title: Brightside Logistics rapid probe notes
body:
Context / quick summary:
- 45m exploratory call with Brightside Logistics (ops + infra + data team) 2024-11-07. They run containerized yard-management and gate-check systems across 12 port terminals (NA + EU). Looking for LLM features to: entity extraction from short OCR snippets, route/freight SLA summarization, and a lightweight assistant for gate agents (low-touch tablet UI).

Primary constraints they repeated:
- Strict network segmentation: customer wants Private deployment on their GCP VPC (no public egress from model runtime).
- Hard latency SLO for gate agent flow: <150ms p50 token latency for short prompts (<=128 tokens) during peak.
- Bursty arrival pattern: short but intense spikes during container offloads (10–20s windows) — planning for 250 concurrent low-latency reqs per terminal when busiest.
- Cost sensitivity: target ~30% lower per-token cost vs their current CPU-based on-prem approach.
- Air-gapped readiness in 6–9mo for a subset of terminals (regulatory).

What they already have:
- Kubernetes clusters at each terminal (k3s on prem), central VPC peering to a staging project, local NFS for artifacts.
- Lightweight OCR pipeline (Tesseract-based) that emits short text snippets (often noisy, lots of abbreviations).
- Tablet web UI used by gate agents; app makes sync calls to a local API.

Redwood fit hypotheses (from call):
- Private deployment with control plane in Redwood but model runtime inside their VPC (Private + onprem bundle) would satisfy segmentation while allowing managed rollouts.
- Use small quantized model family (e.g., 3B q4/8bit) for entity extraction to hit latency and cost targets; fall back to slightly larger variant for ambiguous OCR cases.
- Prefix caching for repeating OCR patterns (plate numbers, container IDs) could cut token count significantly for the most common flows.
- Dedicated batching config: continuous micro-batching to preserve latency at p50 while aggregating at p95.

Notes / gotchas raised live:
- Tablet connectivity: some terminals have flaky LTE; network intermittency may cause replays. Need offline-safe mode: local inference fallback or queueing.
- Security/compliance: security team insists all keys are customer-managed (KMS/HSM). They also asked for explicit audit trail per request (who queried what).
- Model drift concern: their legal/ops teams worried about hallucinated container IDs in summaries — strict extractor-first approach preferred vs free-form summarization.
- Existing OCR errors: short tokens like "C0N" vs "CON" are common. Need robust normalization and a domain lexicon to reduce model fuzziness.

Technical acceptance criteria (customer-specified) — rough:
- Cold-start p50 token latency <= 180ms (they gave 150ms but we scoped up slightly for initial pilot).
- Peak concurrent handling: 250 concurrent small requests/terminal for up to 20s windows without queue loss (scale test).
- No egress: model runtime cannot reach public internet; only control plane -> runtime visible via peered channels.
- Key management: CMEK/KMS for all model keys; logs shipped to their SIEM via syslog.
- Minimal hallucinations: entity-extraction precision >= 95% on their annotated 500-sample test set.

Implementation ideas / architecture sketch (working):
- Private control plane in Redwood (managed) with a Private Connector deployed as k8s DaemonSet per terminal cluster. The runtime image is pulled from their internal registry (or air-gapped tarball for offline sites).
- Model selection: quantized 3B for inference with optional 7B lane for ambiguous cases. Smart routing policy: by confidence score request -> if confidence < 0.6 then route to 7B or a specialized rule-based post-processor.
- Caching: per-terminal prefix/KV cache stored locally (etcd or Redis); keys encrypted with CMEK. TTLs tuned to terminal patterns (short, minutes).
- Batching: continuous batching with micro-batch window 5–15ms; dynamic window expansion during low traffic.
- Offline fallback: lightweight rule-based extractor (JS binary in UI) as safety net when connectivity lost, with queued sync to central for reconciliation.

Open questions (need answers before proposal):
- Licensing: can we ship quantized model binary under customer-managed registry? Need legal check on model redistribution for the selected open model.
- Network: they prefer no inbound prod connections to their clusters; is a reverse-tunnel (controller initiated) acceptable? Security team wants to vet.
- Annotation set: can they provide the 500-sample annotated set by next week (11/15) for accuracy baseline?
- Load simulation: will they provide realistic replay traces of OCR traffic or do we need to synthesize?

Immediate next steps (short timeline):
- Action: Send pilot scope + high-level architecture note to Brightside contact (Marco assigned) — due 2024-11-09. Owner: Priya.
- Action: Legal check on selected model redistribution (Aisha + Legal) — target 2024-11-12.
- Action: Ask Brightside for annotated 500-sample set + representative traffic trace (SFTP link). Marco to request; follow-up 11/08.
- Action: Prepare a quick perf test plan (k3s cluster emulation + 250 concurrent clients) and a cost estimate for 3-month pilot (infra + support). Owner: Eng SRE (TBD).
- Action: Prototype offline extractor JS widget for tablet demo (throwaway, short block) — Priya to hack up a proof-of-concept by 11/13.

Notes to self / internal reminders:
- Emphasize extractor-first approach in proposal (they are risk-averse to hallucinations).
- Quantization profiles: run microbenchmarks on A100 vs T4 equivalents to map latency/cost tradeoff.
- Think about a canary policy that pins one terminal to 7B during early rollout to validate edge cases.
- Add a short paragraph in pilot docs about syslog/siem integration and request sample schema.

Meeting snippets (verbatim-ish):
- Ops lead: "If it takes more than a second to tell me a container ID at gate, it's functionally useless."
- Infra: "We cannot accept IPs from external services to our control plane; anything must be initiated from inside our network."
- Data lead: "We can supply a decent annotated set but want tooling to monitor extraction quality over time — alerts if precision drops 5%+."

Potential risks and mitigations:
- Risk: LTE flakiness causes throughput gaps -> Mitigation: local rule-based fallback + aggressive retry queueing + eventual consistency reconciliation.
- Risk: model redistribution/legal -> Mitigation: propose two options: (1) customer pulls runtime from their registry (preferred), (2) provide signed air-gap image with tighter license review.
- Risk: hallucinations in summaries -> Mitigation: extractor-first pipeline + post-processing validators and guardrails.

Rough stakeholder map:
- Brightside Ops: Caroline H. (primary), gate agent product sponsor
- Brightside Infra/Security: Omar T. (SRE lead)
- Brightside Data: Lucia M. (annotation + metrics)
- Our side: Priya (SE lead), Marco (solutions engineer), Aisha (legal liaison), Eng-SRE (TBD)

Longer-term ask from customer (future phase):
- Air-gapped appliance for terminals classified as high-risk (comms-restricted)
- Integrations with their freight-TMS for contextual enrichment (agent sees ETA + hold codes inline)
- Continuous evals dashboard (per-terminal quality, token cost, latency) — could be Redwood Console feature ask

Random thoughts:
- Might be a nice case study for private low-latency inference at edge if pilot succeeds — emphasize measurable unit-economics improvements (tokens per manifest).
- Consider small on-device tiny-LM for last-resort offline extraction (tiny transformer distilled) — fewer dependencies than JS heuristics.

-- end of note --

Local todo for Priya: draft the pilot SOW skeleton and send to Marco for review by 11/09.
